title: The Influence of Artificial Intelligence Chatbots on Customer Experience, Satisfaction and Brand Loyalty in E-Commerce
content: AI chatbots are making their way into ecommerce as "24/7" on-demand interfaces to guide, resolve, and inquiry. However, its implementation does not promise a better experience or increased brand attachment. We theorize from available research about chatbot property-construals on consumers' experience and satisfaction, and how those experiences lead to retention, repurchase and loyalty. A structured integrative review of peer reviewed empirical articles and reviews, derived mainly from 2020 to November 2026, and the extant literature on customer experience, information-systems success and expectation-confirmation was conducted in which publications were analyzed via thematic comparisons and a study-level matrix; no primary data, pooled effects, or statistical models were studied. Consistently, responsiveness, informational quality, relevance, reliability and service recovery lead to positive end-states; empathy and social presence foster trust, and social cues (such as humanlike appearance) may do so as well. Meta-analyses show that chatbot satisfaction is positively correlated with behavioral intentions but that the relatively large between-studies heterogeneity tempers the generality of these findings. Research in other industries shows that although chatbots can grab consumers' attention, its effects on emotional stimulation are uncertain and technology-induced errors cause cognitive dissonance, with accompanying frustration and reduced service quality ratings. We conclude with an integrative journey framework involving interaction personality-construals, experience, satisfaction and outcomes. Chatbots will be most effective at engendering loyalty if they guide consumers accurately, effectively and with good timing, manage their own capabilities and provide quick escalation procedures when conditions demand.
